The precondition is too weak: both arguments must be positive, so that each subtraction strictly reduces one argument while both stay above zero. This matches the method gcdI, which already requires m > 0 && n > 0 and keeps both x > 0 and g > 0 as invariants, so strengthening the function's precondition still type-checks at all call sites.

The function gcd has only the precondition 'requires m > 0', with n left unconstrained. Restricting index to at most |n.Contents| makes every branch well-defined: for index > n.weight, n.right must be non-null and the recursive index lies within |n.right.Contents|.
